properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 5:29PM MDT until October 25 at 9:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding likely along the Rio Grande between Monte Vista and
Alamosa.

* WHERE...Southeastern Rio Grande County and West Central Alamosa
County...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Rio Grande and low lying agricultural
areas in Rio Grande and Alamosa counties is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 525 PM MDT, Emergency management reports flooding of low lying
areas along and near the Rio Grande in Rio Grande county and in
Alamosa county upstream of the city of Alamosa.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Rio Grande and West Central
Alamosa Counties between Monte Vista and Alamosa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 5:00PM MDT until October 24 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along the Conejos River.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 715 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 457 PM MDT, High water levels in area creeks and streams
continue, although many locations in the San Juan Mountains have
crested and have begun to slowly fall. Over the western portion
of the San Luis Valley, many streams and creeks are near crest
now and will slowly fall for the remainder of the day. The
Conejos River at Mogote has crested, but will likely remain above
flood stage until early Monday morning.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Platoro, Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 4:20PM MDT until October 26 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring. Low-water
crossing are inundated with water and may not be passable. The
river is running fast and high. Do not attempt to cross.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 407 PM MDT, The San Juan River is forecast to crest Sunday
morning between the Four Corners and Bluff, cresting between
Bluff and Mexican Hat Sunday afternoon and peaking at Mexican Hat
by midnight Sunday night.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:49PM MDT until October 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County and Rio Grande County...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue along and near the Rio Grande this
afternoon, especially from near Del Norte to below Monte Vista.
Several roads remain closed and housing areas evacuated due to high
water. While many rivers and streams have crested this morning,
flooding and high flows will continue this afternoon and evening,
especially around Monte Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 340 PM MDT, Water levels along the Rio Grande remain high,
especially in the stretch from Del Norte to below Monte Vista,
although the river has crested and levels are forecast to remain
steady or slowly fall into evening.
- Highway 285 between Monte Vista and Center remains closed, as
well as Highway 112 between Del Norte and Center and Highway 160
between Wolf Creek Pass and South Fork. Please continue to heed
any road closures.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande from Del Norte to Monte Vista.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:31PM MDT until October 25 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southwestern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 329 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported heavy rain in the
warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing Between 2
and 4 inches of rain have fallen since Thursday morning.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. This could cause additional rises within rivers,
creeks and streams.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, Bayfield, Ignacio, La Plata, Falfa, Oxford, Bondad,
Hesperus, Breen, Vallecito, Mayday, Kline, Marvel, Tiffany,
Allison and Redmesa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:47PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

* WHAT...The San Juan River is still running high but expected to
remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. Additional rainfall
could cause the river to rise, but it is expected to continue
decreasing through Sunday.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 10.3 feet, Water is flowing over the yards of homes in
the San Juan River Village northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is currently below minor flood stage but is
expected to remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. It is
expected to continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday morning and 7.3
feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 1:55PM MDT until October 26 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed to Minor severity and increased in
duration for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte, Alamosa...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Minor Flood. The Del Norte Riverwalk Trail
floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 5.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 5.5 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.5
feet on 06/18/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 11:39AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is imminent or ongoing with additional rounds of showers
and thunderstorms expected through Saturday afternoon. Rivers and
creeks may still experience high waters even after rainfall has
ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 4:09PM MDT until October 25 at 10:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Along the Dolores River from Bedrock to the confluence with
the Colorado River in:
Southwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado...
West Central Montrose County in west central Colorado...
East Central Grand County in east central Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Dolores River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 408 PM MDT, Flooding is expected along the Dolores River.
Highway 141 could see impacts along the river as well as the 141
bridge through Gateway. Water levels are forecast to continue to
rise through Gateway this evening and peak overnight. The river
is running fast and high.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dolores River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gateway and Highway 141
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
